reason: E2 supports that laser cladding can produce good coatings on TC4, but provides no evidence for refractory HEA coatings on TC4 or their hardness/wear benefits. E1 shows nano-CeO2 refines grains and improves homogeneity in an FeCoNiCrMo HEA on 316L stainless steel, but the alloy, substrate, and specific outcome (slight decrease in hardness) differ from the hypothesis, leaving the transfer to refractory HEA on TC4 unsupported.
premises: Laser cladding produces low-porosity, crack-free, well-bonded coatings on TC4
Refractory HEA coatings improve hardness and wear resistance over TC4
Nano-CeO2 addition refines grain structure and reduces porosity in HEA coatings
Nano-CeO2 addition improves homogeneity of hardness and wear resistance in HEA coatings
Benefits of nano-CeO2 observed on 316L stainless steel will transfer to TC4 substrate
